paragraphs.text: Forsha et al. (2011) evaluated baseline ECGs and echocardiograms in 87 patients with late-onset Pompe disease (median age 44 years, 51% male, 94% Caucasian; median disease duration 15 years) enrolled in a randomized trial. Overall, 46% had 1 or more ECG or echocardiographic abnormalities: the most common ECG findings were left ventricular hypertrophy (12%) and short PR interval (10%, 90-120 ms); 7% had decreased left ventricular ejection fraction (41-54%), and 5% had elevated left ventricular mass index on echocardiogram, all in the mild range. Other findings included bundle branch block (4%), atrial enlargement (4%), and Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome (2 patients). Severe ventricular hypertrophy classically associated with infantile Pompe disease was not observed, and ECG-defined left ventricular hypertrophy was not specific for increased left ventricular mass: of 10 patients with LVH on ECG, only 1 had elevated LV mass index on echocardiography. No differences were seen between patients with disease duration under versus at least 15 years; 3 of 5 (60%) patients with symptom onset before age 10 had abnormalities. The authors suggested that the abnormalities may be related to Pompe disease or to comorbid conditions.
